findings.detail: The question repeats the problem of M2-S42-T2. Both start from an oversized root CLAUDE.md that mixes testing, API and deployment conventions and is hard to edit. Both ask where to split the content by topic, and both have the same correct action: topic files such as testing.md and api-conventions.md in .claude/rules/. The added constraint (topics apply to every package) only changes the distractor from user-level to directory-level scope. The reasoning that leads to the answer is unchanged, so the question offers no different problem, such as a cause against a fix or a choice between two rules.

blind_answer.reason: .claude/rules/ holds focused, topic-specific rule files as an alternative to a monolithic CLAUDE.md, and they apply project-wide. Option A would limit each topic to one directory. Option B makes always-needed standards on-demand only. Option D leaves files that would not be loaded at all.
